name: Canebrake Wren
rangeDescription: Eastern nicaragua to eastern costa rica and northwestern panama (western bocas del toro)
description: Small, skulking wren of foothills and lowlands along the Caribbean slope from Nicaragua south to western Panama. Found in forest edges, second-growth thickets, and brushy fields with cane grass.

name: Chestnut-capped Piha
rangeDescription: Northern slope of central cordillera of andes of colombia
description: Rare and endangered Colombian endemic restricted to a very small area in the northern part of the central Andes. Fairly large and almost uniformly gray with a faint, yellow eyering.

name: Eastern Kingbird
rangeDescription: Eastern north america; winters mainly western amazon basin
description: Fairly large flycatcher, dark gray above and clean white below with blacker head. Look for white tail tip.

name: Obi Golden-Bulbul
rangeDescription: Obi (northern moluccas)
description: A thrush-sized bird with a heavy bill, olive-green upperparts, and a yellow underside. Particularly note the yellow cheeks and the yellowish patch beside the bill, making the dark eye stand out from the face.

name: Writhe-billed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Central philippines (panay, guimaras, and negros)
description: A large rare bird of lowland and foothill forest on Panay and Negros, although almost extinct on the latter. Mostly black with a cream-colored tail with black terminal band, an orange casque, and a wrinkled lower bill.

name: Natewa Silktail
rangeDescription: Fiji (mountains of vanua levu)
description: Small and stub-tailed, appearing mostly dark. Shows vivid electric blue speckling on chest, back, and head, brilliant blue in direct light.

name: New Britain Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Coastal lowlands of new britain (southeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A medium-sized blue-and-white kingfisher with a pale blue crown, a black eye mask, and a mostly white body with blue wings and tail. Female has blue rump, while male’s is white.

name: Fox's Weaver
rangeDescription: Swamps of east-central uganda
description: A chunky, short-tailed, long-billed weaver. Breeding males are mostly yellow with a black face mask, a pale eye, and a mostly black, yellow-streaked back.

name: African Pied Starling
rangeDescription: Far southeastern namibia to southern mozambique and south africa
description: A large, dark brown starling with upright posture that shows white under the short tail. Up close it has a pale eye, a yellow gape, and a dull greenish sheen on the shoulders.

name: Spotted Bowerbird
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (central queensland to western new south wales and far northwestern victoria)
description: A brownish, mottled, strongly marked bowerbird with warm brown tones overall and a small pink crest on the nape. Loud rasping calls include hisses and squawks.

name: Surf Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Rocky coasts of peru (ancash southward to tacna)
description: Brown thrush-like bird of the Peruvian coastline; it never ventures very far from the ocean. Note the buffy wing markings and white streaking on the throat, though its highly specialized habitat is the best identification feature; any brown land bird foraging at the edge of the sea is likely to be this species.

name: Mindoro Bleeding-heart
rangeDescription: Forest of mindoro (central philippines); status unknown
description: A very rare medium-sized ground dove of lowland and foothill forest floor on Mindoro. Iridescent bluish on the head and back of the neck, with a purplish back, a blackish wing with white triangular marks on the shoulder, a white throat and underparts, and a small red “bleeding heart” in the center of the chest.

name: Sumba Brown Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sumba (lesser sundas)
description: An unremarkable drab, brown flycatcher, gray-brown above and pale below. Note the pale base to the bill.

name: Black-chinned Babbler
rangeDescription: Himalayas (kashmir to central nepal)
description: Small buffy babbler with a black throat and lores. Social, often occurring in flocks with other species.

name: Philippine Collared-Dove
rangeDescription: Philippines and sulu archipelago; vagrant to northern borneo; introduced to northern marianas (guam north to saipan)
description: Brownish dove with a short collar of large dark scales, a gray head, and a pinkish flush on the neck and breast. Native to the Philippines, where now declining and uncommon; fairly common in introduced range (Guam and Northern Mariana Islands).

name: Gunnison Sage-Grouse
rangeDescription: Gunnison basin of southwestern colorado and adjacent southeastern utah
description: Large turkeylike bird found in extensive areas of sagebrush. Both sexes gray overall with very fine patterning, black belly, and long pointed tail.

name: Geelvink Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Numfor, biak, and yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Localized endemic of islands in West Papua’s Geelvink Bay, including Biak and Numfor. Males have a large, bright “fried egg” yellow-and-white patch on the chest and a hot pink patch on the belly.

name: Little Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern thailand, malay peninsula, and greater sundas
description: This aptly-named forest species is the smallest of the green-pigeons. Males are highly distinctive, with a blue-gray head and neck, orange chest, pinkish-maroon back, and green belly.

name: Halmahera Boobook
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (halmahera, ternate, and bacan)
description: A brown owl with a rounded head, yellow eyes, and rufescent barred underparts. Inhabits forest in the lowlands and lower foothills, where it usually occurs in territorial pairs.

name: Milky Stork
rangeDescription: Lowlands of malaya, indochina, greater sundas, and sulawesi
description: Large white stork with a yellow bill and reddish face and legs. Extensive black on the wings and tail only prominent in flight; a little of this black edging on the wings occasionally visible when the bird is foraging.
